answers.explanation: Users care about ease of use and performance. Utilization matters to the people who pay for shared machines.
On a shared machine, one user hogging the CPU slows everyone else down, so fair, efficient sharing is the priority.
Small batteries and limited hardware push mobile OSes to focus on the touch experience and power.
Embedded computers just run their task. They're the most common kind of computer there is.
As resource allocator, the OS shares CPU time, memory, storage, and devices among everyone who wants them.
As control program, the OS stops a buggy or malicious program from damaging the system or other programs.
A workstation user has their own machine, yet their files and printers often live on servers.
Sharing and protecting: the two jobs from the system's view.
